activities.title: I-110 incoming-path convergence and jerk-feasibility diagnostics
activities.question: Can current incoming-lane topology expose late-ramp encounters before leader entry, and does a jerk-bounded stopping profile fit the conditional longitudinal clearance?
activities.why_now: Late-ramp leader entries precede large native braking jerk; prior current-neighbor margins offered no pre-entry ramp warning.

trigger.text: Sam: Let's continue, after the 2 November repository review and roadmap; previous nearest-neighbor margins missed pre-entry ramp warning.

activities.method: Stream current states only; graph reachable non-internal common edges without hypothetical lane changes, pair same/adjacent lane endpoints, select nearest common edge by summed forward distances with deterministic ties. Routes/IDs/event schedule/leader labels cannot select candidates. Signed positions before the anchor yield a conditional projected gap, never a measured bumper gap on different paths. Current Euclidean range 120 m is the information-matched diagnostic; 240 m is an explicitly expanded range. Unreachable/invalid topology and infeasible initial braking states stay unknown. Adjacent paths are possible lateral interactions with unknown intent, not guaranteed convergence. Continuous piecewise-polynomial ego stop: hold current acceleration 0.1 s, jerk -2 to at most -2.5 m/s2, hold as needed, jerk +2 to zero acceleration exactly at zero speed. Reject initial states for which this bounded monotone stopping profile cannot be constructed. Other car either holds current speed or brakes immediately at 9 m/s2 to rest; both are assumptions. Evaluate exact extrema of displacement closure plus h*ego speed, h=0 and 2, including all segment boundaries and polynomial roots. Required gap = 2.5 + maximum of that expression. This constructs a conditional response, not a safety proof or optimal controller.
activities.result: Current topology exposes the two late-ramp targets before leader entry, but the 120 m conditional stopping margins are insufficient in ramp-44 and fragile in ramp-50. Expanded 240 m context offers earlier supported projections; it is an additional information requirement, not demonstrated sensing or a validated control fix. A deficit marks failure of this response profile, not proof that no other response is possible.
activities.limits: One previously inspected synthetic seed; provisional geometry; exact simulator positions and map; expanded 240 m range is not demonstrated sensing/communication. Conditional lateral projection has no merge-time or intent evidence. Braking models are assumptions; other road users, SUMO intervention and delayed insertions are not counterfactually resolved. No rollout, actor, training, protected audit inspection or shared writes.
activities.next_action: Predeclare a bounded preview-control contract: observation range and uncertainty, conditional lateral-path handling, positive braking reserve, other-motion assumptions, recovery and native safety authority. Then test matched development interventions with full controlled/human/ramp/external burdens before any comfort acceptance; keep geometry qualification and v04 handoff separate.

activities.title: Preview v2 braking/recovery against unchanged baseline
activities.question: Does continuous route-local preview remove v1 overbraking/recovery failures without sacrificing comfort, safety or complete-cohort cost?
activities.why_now: V1 adjacent conditional paths caused persistent braking, including cut-in-off. Its stop-oriented latch delayed recovery. Peaks coincide with native ACC mode transition around 100 m; v2 closes speed differences before that transition. Same-path leader observation cannot predict an unannounced instantaneous cut-in; failure remains visible.

trigger.text: Sam requested fixing preview braking/recovery and testing v2 against the same baseline, and asked what happened to the original car.

activities.method: Use current route-local TraCI getLeader within 240 m (120 m sensitivity); do not brake for other vehicles merely on an adjacent possible path. Apply continuous early gap-closing request 0.8*(leader_speed-ego_speed)+0.04*(net_gap-2*ego_speed-10-low_speed_offset), with low_speed_offset=clamp(75/speed-5,0,2) (2 at rest). Take the lower of this and native ACC/cruise request, apply unchanged measured-acceleration comfort filter and v1 terminal-release guard. No latch, dwell or stale target; immediate state-based recovery still bounded by measured jerk. Speed mode31 and native ACC authority remain. No hypothetical followSpeed queries (they may update ACC mode); one original current-state query per command remains. One exact baseline regression; six cases at 240 m and six at 120 m; first primary case repeated before scaling, plus ramp44 and cutin-on primary repeats: 16 bounded simulations. No outcome-driven v2 tuning. This is a combined engineering revision, not a component-causal ablation.
